name: walk-once
title: Walk Once, with Claude
kicker: The only run that costs tokens
html:
Walk Once, with Claude

At each line of the goal
  1. Sync ARTIE fetches the system’s current resource: its state and the forms it offers now
  2. Reason Claude reads the line and the forms, and picks one, with its values
  3. Act ARTIE sends it; the system checks the values against its own form

Claude chooses only among forms on offer. It cannot invent a call.

The one run
20model calls, claude-sonnet-5-5
33,876input tokens; 29,424 read from cache
3,040output tokens
61steps, in 58 s
exhibits/merge-watch-release/capture-release.sh 501   # needs a model key and Jenkins
# walks release.goal.md once, then artie generate keeps it:
#   release.heart.yaml   the script
#   release.pins.yaml    a fingerprint of every form it used
say: That replay had no model in it. The model ran once, before it. ARTIE took the goal line by line. At each system it fetched the current resource, showed Claude the line and the forms on offer, and sent what Claude picked. Claude can only choose among forms a system offers at that moment; it cannot invent a call, and each system checks the values against its own form, the way it would for any client. One run: 20 model calls, about 34 thousand input tokens, most of them read from cache, 61 steps in under a minute. Then artie generate wrote down what happened as a script, and a fingerprint of every form it used.
